info.title: AIContextBuilder.Console
info.description: Roslyn-based .NET tool to generate dense Markdown context for AI/LLM consumption.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: aicb - Roslyn-based .NET Markdown context generator for AI/LLM workflows. (c) Gregor Dadera - free for individuals and small organizations; see LICENSE.txt for the thresholds.

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: -h
options.description: Show help and usage information

commands.name: init
commands.description: Wire aicb into this project for an MCP client: add the aicb entry to .mcp.json, write the agent skills to .claude/skills/, and install the symbol guard for the agent harnesses this project uses. Existing files are kept unless --force.

options.name: --path
options.description: Project directory to wire up. Default: the current directory.

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite artefacts that are already there. Without it an existing aicb entry or skill file is left untouched, which is what makes re-running safe.

options.name: --skills
options.description: Which agent skills to write: `context` (default) for aicb-csharp-context only, or `all` to add the aicb-code-review / aicb-code-simplifier review pair.

options.name: --hooks
options.description: Which agent harnesses to install the aicb symbol guard for: `auto` (default) for the ones already used in this project, `none`, `all`, or one of `claude-code` / `codex` / `opencode`.

commands.name: analyze
commands.description: Run Roslyn analysis on a solution and emit context Markdown.

options.name: --solution
options.description: Path to the .sln file of the solution to analyze.

options.name: --output
options.description: Path for the generated context Markdown.

options.name: --session-db
options.description: Path to an existing SQLite session DB. On a hash match the snapshot mode is enabled (skips the Roslyn re-run).

options.name: --emit-session-db
options.description: Path at which the SQLite session DB is written after the run. Created if it does not exist.

options.name: --force
options.description: Bypass the snapshot mode and always run a full Roslyn analysis.

options.name: --layer-profile
options.description: Path to a layer-mapping profile JSON. Default: role-based heuristic.

options.name: --run-template
options.description: Id of a RunTemplate for the MD generation (built-in or custom). Applied by both 'analyze' AND 'export' (template-driven rendering via the UI export path). Without a value: full default render (byte-identical).

options.name: --fail-on
options.description: Opt-in quality gate: if the expression matches, the exit code is 6 (the MD is still generated). Example: "critical>0 OR debt>120min". Metrics: critical/warning/info/ok, debt, complexity-max, ce-max, ca-max, methods, types. Operators: > >= < <= = !=, combinable with AND/OR.

options.name: --format
options.description: Inner notation of the .md file - two ways of writing the same content: 'tag' (the established AI-Builder tag markdown) or 'yaml' (idiomatic YAML). Pick whichever the model or tool that reads the file handles better. Without --format the OutputFormat configured on the RunTemplate is used (template-less: yaml). The file name stays .md.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Re-render Markdown from an existing session DB without a Roslyn re-run.

options.name: --session-db
options.description: Path to the existing session DB from which the context MD is re-rendered (no Roslyn run).

options.name: --output
options.description: Path for the generated context Markdown.

options.name: --run-template
options.description: Id of a RunTemplate for the MD generation (built-in or custom). Applied by both 'analyze' AND 'export' (template-driven rendering via the UI export path). Without a value: full default render (byte-identical).

options.name: --solution
options.description: For a session DB with multiple analyzed solutions, selects the one to render: exact full path, solution name (file name without .sln) or file name, otherwise a substring match on the path (all case-insensitive). Without a value the multi case is a user error with a listing.

options.name: --format
options.description: Inner notation of the .md file - two ways of writing the same content: 'tag' (the established AI-Builder tag markdown) or 'yaml' (idiomatic YAML). Pick whichever the model or tool that reads the file handles better. Without --format the OutputFormat configured on the RunTemplate is used (template-less: yaml). The file name stays .md.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Import a constellation JSON into a target DB (templates / presets / constellations).

options.name: --file
options.description: Path to the constellation JSON file to import.

options.name: --mode
options.description: SkipExisting | Replace - behavior on id conflicts.

options.name: --db-path
options.description: Path to the target SQLite DB for the import - the master-entity/config DB (NOT a session snapshot DB). Created if it does not exist.

options.name: --preview
options.description: Dry run: only show the per-section preview (new/conflict/unchanged/built-in), write nothing.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List built-in + custom master entities (run-templates / detail-presets / model-profiles).

options.name: --json
options.description: JSON output instead of a table.

options.name: --db-path
options.description: Optional source DB. Without a value only the built-ins are listed (fresh temporary DB, discarded afterwards).

arguments.name: KIND
arguments.description: Master-entity type, e.g. run-templates, detail-presets, model-profiles, prompts, context-templates (the full list appears for an unknown kind).

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Start the MCP server (Model Context Protocol, stdio JSON-RPC) - for Claude Code / Cursor / Cline. With --db-path profile-aware (render slots + tool set + skill from the active MCP profile); --mcp-profile pins which profile that is, for this process only.

options.name: --db-path
options.description: Optional master/config DB. Makes the MCP server profile-aware: export_markdown renders through the active MCP profile (slot templates), the tool set follows its ToolSelection, the skill shapes the server instructions. Without a value: full default render + lean-core tools.

options.name: --mcp-profile
options.description: Pin the active MCP profile for this server process by id (see 'list_mcp_profiles', or the MCP Profiles panel in the GUI). Process-local: it does NOT change the profile persisted in the config DB. Without a value the persisted active profile applies. An unknown id aborts the start (the valid ids are listed on stderr).

commands.name: call
commands.description: Invoke ONE MCP tool once and print its result - no stdio JSON-RPC server. For post-rebuild live-validation of any tool (incl. new / non-default-pool ones). Example: aicb call find_usages --sln C:/repo/App.sln --arg symbol=OrderService.

options.name: --sln
options.description: Absolute .sln path - bound to the tool's sessionId/solutionPath argument (self-init analyzes it once). Omit for a tool that needs no session (e.g. server_info).

options.name: --arg
options.description: A tool argument as name=value (repeatable), e.g. --arg symbol=OrderService --arg includeTests=true. Values convert to the parameter type (bool/int/enum/string[]); a complex argument is JSON, e.g. --arg queries='[{"tool":"find_usages",...}]'.

options.name: --db-path
options.description: Optional config DB (same as the GUI): DB-defaulting tools + self-init apply its per-solution config. Without a value the tool runs DB-free.

arguments.name: TOOL
arguments.description: The MCP tool name to invoke, e.g. find_usages, find_production_dead, server_info.
